review_scope: Registered-source content review of arXiv:2401.12331v2, stamped 27 March 2024, by T. Tony Cai, Dongwoo Kim and Hongming Pu. All 25 PDF pages belong to the main paper. Section 6 contains main-paper proofs; page 23 describes a separate supplement, which was not opened. References and author addresses end on page 25. Fresh text evidence covers all 25 pages, and relevant theorem and source-passage pages were inspected visually.
inventory: Independent enumeration finds eight actual Theorem headings: 2.1 (page 6), 2.2 (8), 2.3 (9), 2.4 (12), 3.1 (12), 3.2 (13), 3.3 (14), 3.4 (17). Theorems 2.2, 3.1 and 3.2 continue onto the next page. Their complete bodies and estimator-domain clauses are preserved. Propositions, proof headings and citations are excluded.
original_statements: Theorem 2.1 retains the explicit no-source setting, deterministic target grid with endpoint gap bound, tilde minimax rate and all-target-estimator quantifier. Theorem 3.1 retains its target-only context and estimator clause on page 13, along with the two-sided target density bounds and independent-design minimax rate.

Theorem 2.2 preserves both common-grid gap bounds, the source endpoint indexed by m_t+1 as printed, all degrees, reciprocal-ceiling bandwidths and thresholds, the non-strict/strict oracle selection split and both R_C definitions.

Theorem 3.2 preserves both density lower and upper bounds, degree requirements, all three bandwidth ceilings and caps, including K in the source terms, both thresholds, oracle comparison and every factor in the R_I definitions.

Theorems 2.3 and 3.3 quantify arbitrary estimators from available target and source data. The latter retains the final source index ell as printed. Neither lower-bound statement acquires a named algorithm, upper-bound tuning restrictions or extra design regularity.

Theorems 2.4 and 3.4 retain inherited assumptions, their distinct adaptive algorithms, arbitrary positive repetition counts, complete averaging formulas and their respective inherited rate expressions.
source_passages: All 14 source entries and 12 auxiliary passages were checked. The target/source random functions, noisy observations and pointwise means retain the source independence wording without inserting zero-mean errors or design independence. Balanced counts are constant within target/source groups, not equated across the two groups.

The bounded Holder class uses the largest integer strictly below alpha. Mean and difference functions have separate positive smoothness parameters with no imposed ordering in the model. Assumption 1 is a pointwise tail bound with a common proxy, not a supremum-norm bound; its source-only terms are not prerequisites of the target-only experiment.

The full law-class paragraph and its explicitly stated no-source applications remain distinct. D17 preserves the whole original paragraph and labels the target-only application; its projection convention is separately recorded as not formally defined by the source. Common and independent sampling designs are not combined.

Algorithm 1 retains the packing/covering radii, subject-level random observation selection, free q in the fit, check-marked polynomial coefficients and fit, and intervalwise discard-to-zero thresholding. A magnified crop confirmed the fit notation. Algorithm 2 retains pooled source fitting, target residual fitting and addition.

Algorithm 3 uses 2n_t target subjects, a subject-level split, two fits and spacing-weighted held-out loss. Algorithm 4 uses its own candidate collection, printed positive dyadic grids, duplicate M_s assignment and unweighted held-out loss. The two algorithms are kept separate, with all steps preserved.

R_C and R_I are local scalar rate definitions at the two named candidates; their complete source formulas and inherited specifications are archived for the adaptive statements. They are not reinterpreted as general risk functionals. The L2 loss and asymptotic conventions are resolved in the separate ambient record.
dependency_review: 36 direct uses and 68 deduplicated related connections. Checked every direct list and all 14 related-theorem sets. Source observation D2 and full transfer class D7 reach only the six transfer-setting theorems. D17 reaches only the two target-only minimax results. Algorithms 1/2 and the conventional wrapper reach only the four upper/adaptive results, not the four all-estimator minimax/lower-bound statements. D14 and D16 reach only their respective adaptive theorem. The common and independent designs each reach their own four theorems.
names_and_highlights: Every entry retains natural-language source terms, source types, original source statements and matching selectors. Adjacent naming contexts for mean/difference functions, conventional learning and the conventional setup were checked. Assumption 1 remains an assumption, designs and regularity remain conditions, and algorithm headings are not relabeled as numbered definitions. Selector occurrence and its mathematical correspondence were both checked.
source_limitations: The 18 existing source notes were checked. They retain the noise-centering and independence omissions, conventional model projection, pointwise tail scope, smoothness-degree and threshold overloads, endpoint/index inconsistencies, bandwidth slash scope, packing/covering existence, empty interval draws, selection conventions, impossible little-o mesh, positive dyadic grids, duplicate threshold and density-constant mismatch. These notes do not modify quotations or certify the source claims.
changes: No census-content correction was needed. The per-paper rebuild uses the fixed verified PDF and reconstructs all six extracted artifacts independently of old cached paths. The finalizer docstring now correctly says eight theorems. Earlier scripts are archived and historical review records are preserved.
validation: The inventory and census pass separate validator calls; six rebuilt files match saved bytes exactly. PDF identity, exact heading enumeration, continuation pages, graph checks, source/highlight checks and artifact hashes supplement the manual content review.
